name: Free market
summary: The free market is the ideal of an economy in which prices, wages and output are set by voluntary exchange and competition, with government limited to law, property, money and a few public goods. Advocates argue that prices carry dispersed knowledge that no planner can match, that economic freedom underpins political freedom, and that tariffs, price controls, licensing and state direction of investment generally backfire.
scope: The mainstream pro-market tradition as set out by Adam Smith, Friedrich Hayek and Milton Friedman and summarised in Econlib and Wikipedia. It is an economic doctrine, so social, cultural and foreign-policy statements are mostly neutral or low-confidence inferences. It excludes anarcho-capitalism's private defence and courts, Georgist and market-socialist uses of free markets, and critics such as Polanyi.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Hayek advocated denationalising money with competing private currencies, while Friedman wanted the central bank kept and bound to a money-supply rule.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rothbard says each person specialises in what they do best and that money makes the modern division of labour and its latticework of exchanges possible.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rothbard says the modern latticework of exchanges is made possible by money and that workers are paid in money voluntarily exchanged for their labour.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Prohibiting a class of voluntary exchanges is a centralised intervention that Britannica's definition excludes and Rothbard says hampers market exchange.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Rothbard describes work for a corporation as a voluntary exchange of labour services for a salary, to which both sides agree.

bound-labor.rationale: Rothbard says in a free market every person has a property right over their own labour and can contract freely for it, and that slavery violates it.

central-planning.rationale: Econlib's biography says Hayek showed that planners cannot have the dispersed knowledge individuals hold, and Rothbard says a socialist planning board without prices cannot calculate costs or invest capital.

common-currency.rationale: Econlib's biography says Friedman argued for freely floating exchange rates, which assumes separate currencies.

conscription.rationale: Friedman opposed the draft and lobbied to end it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Econlib's Hayek biography and Rothbard argue that a state-planned economy cannot work, so they do not hold it should be defended against a market economy.

delink-world-market.rationale: Rothbard describes the free market and free price system as making goods from around the world available to consumers, which an end to economic ties with rich countries would cut.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Britannica excludes tariffs and quotas from a free market and Rothbard says it makes goods from around the world available, so a bloc closed to outside trade is rejected.

farm-price-support.rationale: Guaranteeing farmers against price swings is a government price intervention, which Britannica's definition excludes and Rothbard says hampers market exchange.

free-trade.rationale: Rothbard says trade is positive-sum because both parties gain, refuting the argument against free trade, and that free markets make goods from around the world available.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Rothbard says prices are set by how each participant values the goods and by supply and demand, not by the labour embodied in them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Econlib's biography says Hayek held that moral and religious ideals are not proper objects of coercion.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rothbard calls market socialism a contradiction in terms, since socialism means government ownership of the means of production, which leaves no market in capital goods.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Econlib's biography says Hayek argued that the free market gives maximum latitude to use information only individuals have, and Rothbard's entry says price-guided exchange steers investment and production to the proper paths.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Econlib's biography says Friedman argued in Capitalism and Freedom for a negative income tax.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Britannica excludes tariffs, quotas and similar interventions, and Rothbard names restrictions that keep new competitors out as government coercion that hampers markets.

no-central-bank.rationale: Hayek advocated denationalising money with competing private currencies, while Friedman wanted the central bank kept and bound to a money-supply rule.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Rothbard lists price controls among government coercions that hamper and cripple market exchanges, and Britannica counts such interventions as absent from a free market.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Rothbard says price controls hamper and cripple market exchanges, which contradicts calling them a good tool.

production-for-use.rationale: Rothbard presents profit-and-loss incentives as what guides production to satisfy consumers, so replacing profit as the purpose of production runs against his account.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rothbard says exploitation occurs not in the free market, where exchanges are voluntary and both sides gain, but where a coercer exploits a victim.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rothbard calls the security of private property rights the key to the existence and flourishing of the free market, and answers critics that property rights are human rights.

public-ownership.rationale: Rothbard says the free market rests on private property titles and that under government ownership of the means of production there can be no real market in land or capital goods.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Rothbard treats wages as the price of labour services agreed voluntarily and lists price controls among government coercions that hamper exchanges, so a legal wage floor is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Britannica defines the free market as one where quality controls, taxes, quotas and other centralised economic interventions are absent or minimal, which excludes strict regulation of firms.

rent-control.rationale: Rent ceilings are price controls, which Rothbard says hamper and cripple market exchanges.

school-vouchers.rationale: Econlib's biography says Friedman argued in Capitalism and Freedom for education vouchers.

self-ownership.rationale: Rothbard says in a free-market system every person has a property right over their own person and labour.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Rothbard says profit-and-loss signals guide capital investment into the proper paths and that planners lacking prices cannot invest capital, and Econlib's biography reports Hayek's argument that planners lack the on-the-ground information.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Britannica lists tariffs and quotas among the interventions absent from a free market, and Rothbard calls arguments against free trade a mercantilist fallacy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Econlib's biography says Hayek objected to progressive taxation because it violates equality before the law.

total-state.rationale: Econlib's biography quotes Hayek that economic control is control of the means for all our ends and says he argued government control of economic life amounts to totalitarianism.

trade-surplus.rationale: Rothbard rejects the mercantilist view that one trading party gains only at the other's expense, on which aiming for an export surplus rests.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: Rothbard says saving and investment in a free market raise workers' productivity and wages and thereby their standard of living.
